_meta.indication: Prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of cancer chemotherapy, including, but not limited to, highly emetogenic chemotherapy

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, parallel group superiority study with a multiple-cycle safety extension
pivotal_trials.population: Cancer patients scheduled to receive the first cycle of anthracycline and cyclophosphamide (AC) based moderately emetogenic chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete response (no emetic episode and no rescue medication) in the delayed phase (25-120 hours) at Cycle 1
pivotal_trials.n: 1455 patients randomized; 1450 received study medication (Akynzeo n=725; palonosetron n=725)
pivotal_trials.result: Superiority demonstrated for CR in the delayed phase: 76.9% vs 69.5% (OR 1.48, 95% CI 1.16 to 1.87; p=0.001); also significant in acute (88.4% vs 85.0%, p=0.047) and overall phases (74.3% vs 66.6%, p=0.001)

nct_ctgov.title: An Efficacy and Safety Study of Oral Netupitant and Palonosetron for the Prevention of Nausea and Vomiting

pivotal_trials.phase: Originally designed as a Phase 2 dose-ranging study, used as pivotal evidence of NETU+PALO efficacy in HEC
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel group, dose-ranging (1:1:1:1) multicenter study of netupitant 100/200/300 mg with palonosetron and dexamethasone versus palonosetron alone
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with solid tumor malignancy scheduled to receive first course of cisplatin-based (>=50 mg/m2) highly emetogenic chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Protocol-specified primary endpoint was complete response (no emetic episodes, no rescue medication) in the overall phase (0-120 hours)
pivotal_trials.n: 694 patients randomized, 679 received study medication (PALO alone N=136; PALO+NETU 100 mg N=135; 200 mg N=137; 300 mg N=135)
pivotal_trials.result: CR in overall phase (0-120 hours): netupitant 300 mg 89.6% vs palonosetron alone 76.5% (difference 13.2%, p=0.003 by CMH); all netupitant doses statistically superior with differences ranging 10.9% to 13.2%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=3% and greater than palonosetron) are headache, asthenia, dyspepsia, fatigue, constipation and erythema. In HEC Cycle 1 (N=136): dyspepsia 4% vs 2%, fatigue 4% vs 2%, constipation 3% vs 1%, erythema 3% vs 2%. In AC-based MEC Cycle 1 (N=725): headache 9% vs 7%, asthma 8% vs 7%, fatigue 7% vs 5%.
target_moa: Fixed combination of netupitant, a substance P/neurokinin 1 (NK1) receptor antagonist, and palonosetron, a serotonin-3 (5-HT3) receptor antagonist
modality: small molecule (oral fixed-combination of two small molecules; netupitant is a new molecular entity NK1 antagonist, palonosetron a 5-HT3 antagonist)

summary.text: Akynzeo was submitted as an NDA under section 505(b) and received September 27, 2013, with standard review. It is the first fixed combination of an NK1 receptor antagonist (netupitant, a new molecular entity) and a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist (palonosetron). Approval was based on full (not accelerated) review; no advisory committee was convened because it is not first-in-class.
